Redundancy is per side - front/rear 1 and 4 - with an LC Switch behind both.","kind":"example"},"docsis-non-redundant":{"bays":{"front-0":"casa/us-16x8@1","front-1":"casa/us-16x8@1","front-2":"casa/smm-8x10g@1","front-3":"casa/smm-8x10g@1","front-4":"casa/ds-8x96@1","front-5":"casa/ds-8x96@1","pem-1":"casa/c40g-pem@1","pem-2":"casa/c40g-pem@1","rear-0":"casa/rfu-16x8@1","rear-1":"casa/rfu-16x8@1","rear-2":"casa/blank-faceplate@1","rear-3":"casa/blank-faceplate@1","rear-4":"casa/rfd@1","rear-5":"casa/rfd@1"},"description":"Non-redundant chassis. The guide: \"The Casa C40G chassis is available in both redundant and non-redundant versions.\" There are no switch modules at all - rear 2 and 3 carry blank filler plates where the redundant schemes carry the SMM Switch pair, and rear 1 and 4 carry I/O rather than an LC Switch. Front DS cards pair with QAM IO behind them and front US cards with US IO, which is the classic split architecture rather than the BDM one.","kind":"orderable"}},"datasheet":{"sha256":"9c74d11413d9dc226900e1372a18ea4e3b6617efe96793356694b9ff3c841cc3","title":"Casa Systems C40G Converged Cable Access Platform data sheet"},"description":"Casa C40G CMTS/CCAP - 6RU, 6 paired front/rear slots. Takes the same line cards as the C100G but HORIZONTALLY, so the card is one model placed at rotate 90.","format":1,"gaps":[{"note":"THE ORDERING SHEET SELLS FOUR CHASSIS AND THIS LIBRARY MODELS TWO. C40G_DS_RevA lists C40G-CHASSIS-AC and C40G-CHASSIS-DC, which are here, and C40G-CHASSIS-ACR and C40G-CHASSIS-DCR, described as \"with Redundant Power and Cooling\", which are not. The sheet gives the phrase and nothing else - no count, no which modules, no dimensions - and the installation guide never uses the word for a chassis variant. What the guide DOES say is that the C40G takes up to four 1100 W PSUs operating concurrently and that fewer than two cannot power a C40G-20, which tells you the supplies are redundant by population rather than by chassis. That makes the R variants most likely a populated bundle rather than different metal - but \"most likely\" is not a source, and inventing two configurations from a four-word description would put a guess where a part number goes.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["ac-power","dc-power","power","fans"],"wanted":"a Casa or CommScope ordering guide saying what the R bundles contain - how many PSUs and fan modules, and whether the chassis itself differs at all","what":"redundant-power-and-cooling-variants"},{"blocks":[],"note":"Casa says two things about this terminal and they do not agree. The prose in \"Connecting the chassis to ground\" says it \"provides two M6 screws to connect a double-lug ground terminal cable\". Figures 1-2 and 1-4 both DRAW three studs, in a 2x2 grid with the protective-earth mark in the fourth corner, and the two figures agree with each other. THE DRAWING IS FOLLOWED, and the model carries three. The figure is the only source that says anything about arrangement at all, so following the prose would mean inventing a layout for the two it describes; and a third stud has easy explanations - a spare, an alternate lug pitch - while a stud drawn twice that is not there has none. That is a judgement, not a reading, which is why it is filed here. THE PITCH IS NOT MEASURED FROM EITHER. It is borrowed from casa/ground-bolts@1, 15.3, off the maintainer`s hand-built C100G rear SVG. Figure 1-4 gives 13.2 across and 14.7 down for what must be one square grid - an 11 percent disagreement with itself, which is that figure`s anisotropy rather than a rectangular pattern.","reason":"sources-disagree","scope":["ground-studs-rear"],"wanted":"a photograph of the C40G rear lower-left corner, which would settle the count and the pitch together in one look","what":"ground-stud-count"},{"blocks":[],"note":"The card band runs 37.5 to 386.7 in a body 432.95 wide, so it sits 37.5 from the left edge and 46.25 from the right - 8.75 mm out of centre, or 4.375 on the band's own centreline. Everything inside the band agrees with everything else; the question is whether the band is really off-centre in the metal, and nothing we hold answers it. IT IS NOT COSMETIC, and the AC input panel is where it bites. Its four C14 inlets sit behind the four front power supplies. Reflect the supply centres about the PANEL and the inlets are 1.2 out; reflect them about the CHASSIS - which is what walking round a box actually does - and they are 9.95 out. The gap between those two answers IS this asymmetry, and no arrangement of the parts inside the band can close it, because the disagreement is between the band and the chassis rather than within either. THE SUPPORTING NUMBERS ARE ALSO ODD IN THE SAME DIRECTION. The two front fan strips measure 36.0 wide each - equal, as you would expect - but leave 1.5 outside them on the left and 10.25 on the right. Two equal strips with unequal surrounds is exactly the shape of a band that has been positioned from one edge. NOT RESOLVED BY GUESSING, deliberately. Re-centring the band would move the two fan strips, the card bays on both faces, the PSU row, the PSU cover and the AC panel - and it would be one estimate reconciled against another, which this device's `pem-band-top-edge` note already records going wrong twice in opposite directions.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["front","rear"],"wanted":"a dimensioned C40G front or rear elevation from Casa, or a tape measure across a real chassis from its left edge to the first card slot and from the last card slot to its right edge","what":"band-not-centred-in-chassis"},{"note":"The PEM band's BOTTOM edge at 264.5 is agreed by every source and is not in doubt. Its TOP edge is known only to about 2 mm, and the three candidates each have support: 194.0 is the direct reading of Figure 1-4 and is impossible, because the card slot above ends at 194.82; 194.82 is flush against that slot; 196.0 is what the bays carry and is what the manifest now uses, on the argument that 194.82 is an accumulation of six DERIVED slot pitches (426.6 mm over 14 slots on the C100G, carried across) and that the front face shows a measured 1.48 mm margin in the equivalent position. That argument is sound but it is an argument, not a measurement, and the whole disagreement is six pixels at 2.982 px/mm. A tape measure on a real C40G, or any Casa drawing that dimensions the rear panel, would settle it in one number. FIGURE 1-12 HAS NOW BEEN LOOKED AT AND DOES NOT SETTLE IT, recorded so nobody spends the search twice. \"C40G power entry module\" is the only isolated drawing of this part and the first independent look anything has had at it. Its body measures 866 x 381 px for an aspect of 2.273. The modelled 158.0 x 68.5 is 2.307 and the superseded 158.0 x 70.5 is 2.241, and 2.273 lands 0.04 percent off the midpoint of those two - at 158.0 wide it implies a height of 69.51. IT IS EQUIDISTANT AND CONFIRMS NEITHER. This guide's isolated part drawings are in any case demonstrably about 10 percent wrong about their own aspect - Figure 1-20 draws a card at 12.54 whose real aspect is 11.34 - so a 1.5 percent lean is well inside the drawing's own error. THE NUMBER IS THEREFORE NOT MOVED. It has been moved twice already, in both directions, and a third move on evidence that splits the difference would be the reconciliation loop rather than an escape from it. What Figure 1-12 does confirm is the ARRANGEMENT, which is what a figure is good for: a bolted terminal cover across the top with three fasteners, a minus pair of studs above a plus pair inside two outlined blocks, two release levers standing proud of the body top and bottom, and the yellow disconnect-power label to their right - all of which casa/c40g-pem draws. RECORDED BECAUSE THE MODULE AND THE BAY NOW AGREE, which means nothing will ever flag this again - the fit check that found the original 2 mm discrepancy is satisfied by both being wrong together as easily as by both being right.","reason":"needs-drawing","scope":["pem-1","pem-2"],"wanted":"a dimensioned C40G rear elevation, or a tape measure on the PEM opening","what":"pem-band-top-edge"},{"note":"The BDM2/BDM2m datasheet states \"Total Power 300 W\" in a technical specifications table headed \"BDM2/2 m with 6+12 IO Card\", whose RF connector row describes that card's six downstream and twelve upstream ports. The figure is the assembly's. A BDM position is TWO modules here - casa/bdm in a front bay and casa/io-6p12 in the paired rear bay, which is why casa/bdm already carries `pairs-with` - and no document we hold divides the 300 W between them. Writing it onto the front module would make the chassis total come out right and the answer to \"what does a BDM front module draw\" come out wrong, so neither half carries a figure and the chassis total stays a floor. The arithmetic does not settle it either way: 12 x 300 W lands on the C100G's stated 3.6 kW whether the 300 W is the pair or the front half with small rear cards. THE THREE REAR RF I/O CARDS ADDED LATER FALL ON THE SAME SIDE OF THIS AS THE 6+12. casa/rfd, casa/rfu-16x8 and casa/ups-32x4 carry NO power figure, because Tables A-8 and A-9 give their port counts and connector types and no watts at all, and every figure Casa does publish for the slot is already the pair's - Table A-3 heads the DQM column \"Maximum consumption with I/O module\" and Table A-4 gives \"Single DCU w/ RFU I/O\" 200 W against \"Single DCU w/ RFU UPS 32x4 I/O\" 220 W for the same US16x8. Subtracting one from the other to get a rear card's share would be our arithmetic and would also be the wrong subtraction - the 20 W is the difference between two PAIRINGS, not between two I/O cards.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["casa/bdm2@1","casa/bdm2m@1","casa/bdm@1","casa/ds-8x192@1","casa/ds-8x8@1","casa/ds-8x96@1","casa/io-6p12-io2@1","casa/io-6p12-sw-io2@1","casa/io-6p12-sw@2","casa/io-6p12@2","casa/rfd@1","casa/rfu-16x8@1","casa/ups-32x4@1","casa/us-16x4@1","casa/us-16x8@1"],"wanted":"a pairable unit that can carry properties, so that a figure measured on a pair can be attached to the pair. The scope is now DATA - every card here declares `power-draw-scope: module-with-paired-io`, so a chassis sum knows not to add the rear partner and L30 catches it if one gains its own figure - but the scope says only THAT the figure covers a pair, not WHICH pair. The C100G HIG gives the same US16x8 200 W with the RFU I/O and 220 W with the RFU UPS 32x4, and the manifest can carry only one of them. Asking for \"a per-module figure\" was the wrong question: Casa states none, and one may not exist to be divided out. What is missing is the mechanism, and enough vendors doing this to design one from - Casa is the only one in the corpus.","what":"paired-module-power"},{"blocks":[],"note":"Casa rates a power ENTRY module in amps and volts, never in watts. Table A-1 gives \"DC current 20A nominal per feed @ -48VDC\" and the PEM section says the modules \"receive -40.5 to -60 VDC (-48VDC nominal) power from separate 20A power supply sources\" - but no document states a wattage, and deriving one means choosing a point the vendor left open: two current figures across a voltage range put V x I anywhere from about 810 W to 1800 W per feed. A power entry module also does not convert or regulate; it filters and distributes what the plant feeds it, so its rating is a current-carrying limit rather than the continuous output power-output-w means. The stated volts and amps are recorded in the contract's attrs; the L27 warning stays standing as the record that the watt figure is missing.","reason":"vendor-silent","scope":["casa/c40g-pem@1"],"wanted":"a wattage for the C40G power entry module from Casa - a nameplate photograph of the module itself would do it, or any document that rates it in watts rather than amps","what":"power-entry-rating"}],"groups":{"cooling":{"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"Fan module"},"front-slots":{"index-origin":1,"role":"traffic","term":"Slot"},"furniture":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Item"},"grounding":{"index-origin":1,"role":"furniture","term":"Point"},"power":{"attrs":{"redundancy":"n+1","redundancy-note":"n+1. The C40G ships as two power variants and this group holds the bays for both: the AC chassis carries four front PSUs at n+1, the DC chassis two rear PEMs at 1+1 (HIG: wire the second PEM to a secondary supply for redundant power applications). Which bays are populated is a property of the configuration, not of the group"},"index-origin":1,"role":"service","term":"PEM"},"rear-slots":{"index-origin":1,"role":"traffic","term":"Slot"}},"kind":"device","lint":{"waive":{"L44":"the field is 100% buried in 2D and that is correct - the two PEM openings fill this band on a DC chassis and the bolted AC panel covers it on an AC one. It is kept because `vent: 50` is what punches the rear panel in 3D, and a PEM is removable, so the air path behind it is exactly what you see when one is pulled. Delete this waiver if the 3D vent is ever driven from somewhere else."}},"manufacturer":"Casa Systems","maturity":"modelled","model":"C40G","name":"c40g","portfolio":{"family":"CMTS/CCAP"},"profile":"networking","provenance":{"ac-variant":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - the C40G ships AC or DC and the guide draws the rear both ways: Figures 1-2 and 1-3 for the AC chassis, 1-4 and 1-5 for the DC one. The AC build puts \"up to four removable 1100W AC power supply units\" in a row across the bottom FRONT, behind the snap-on cover, in place of the two DC power entry modules at the bottom rear. Figure 1-10 shows them with the cover off and Figure 1-11 shows their other end. Numbering runs right to left - \"PSUs are labeled on the front of the chassis as PSU1, PSU2, PSU3 and PSU4 from right to left\" - so the LEFTMOST bay is psu-4, and rel-pos follows the vendor rather than the drawing order. THIS IS AN ORTHOGONAL AXIS to the other two configurations, which are redundancy schemes: an AC chassis can run either scheme. Configurations are the only mechanism the format has for a variant, so the axes share one list; ac-power changes nothing about redundancy and neither BDM scheme says anything about power. The PEM bays therefore default EMPTY and each DC scheme names them, because a configuration cannot clear a bay - occupants are strings - and because neither AC nor DC is \"the\" C40G. THE AC REAR FACE IS NOW PLACED, and the band is no longer two empty bays. Figures 1-2 and 1-3 show it: one bolted panel across the bottom of the rear carrying a rocker switch and an IEC C14 inlet per PSU, where the DC chassis carries its two PEMs. It was modelled as casa/c40g-ac-inlet-panel@1 and left unplaced because the format could not say that a bolted panel is present in only one configuration - a configuration carried bays, skins, airflow, region-context and part-numbers, but not placements. `only-in` says it, on the placement and on the two PEM bays alike, because which configurations a piece of METAL exists in is a statement about geometry and geometry lives in the view. An AC chassis has the panel and no PEM openings; a DC chassis has the two openings and no panel. They are never both present, so there is no overlap for L13 to reject and no need for a bay to claim one. WHAT THIS FIXED, reported from the viewer: the AC rear drew two black rectangles where the PEM bays sat empty, and selecting one offered casa/c40g-pem - a DC power entry module - as the only thing that could go in a chassis ordered for AC."},"band-alignment":{"note":"REPORTED FROM THE VIEWER twice - the AC panel sitting left with a dark sliver past its right edge, then the front looking \"off kilter\" the same way - and it was ONE error in one number, repeated fourteen times. THE BAND IS 37.5 TO 386.7, 349.2 WIDE, and three independent things in this model already said so: the two front fan strips end and start exactly there, the PSU cover measures 349.2 at 37.5, and the AC input panel measures the same. Figure 1-1, the one front figure that PASSES the orthographic gate, puts the card faces at 37.49 and 386.66 when read at this file`s own calibration. THE CARD BAYS WERE THE OUTLIER, at 42.0 - 2.65 right of centre. That put 4.5 of dead space at the left of the band and pushed the cards 0.8 PAST the right side strip, which is why every full-width part looked shifted against them. THE CARD IS NOT RESIZED, and that is the whole reason the fix is a position and not a width. 345.5 is the card`s own length and it is SHARED with the C100G, where the same parts stand vertically - so the 3.7 difference between card and band is margin, 1.85 a side, not a mismeasured card. The bays move to 39.35 and the card sits centred in its opening. THE LEFT STRIPS STOPPED AT 40.0, 2.5 inside the band, on both faces. Now 37.5, where the front fan strip already ended. A WRONG FIX WAS MADE FIRST AND IS RECORDED because the reasoning is the useful part: the AC panel was moved to 42.0 and narrowed to 345.5 to line up with the cards, and the right strip pushed to 387.5 to stop them overlapping it. That did make the rear self-consistent, by moving the one part that was measured correctly to match thirteen that were not. It is reverted. Aligning to the majority is not the same as aligning to the evidence."},"chassis":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"datasheet - Table A-1 of the C40G Hardware Installation Guide (rev 07/07/2022): 10.47in (265.90mm) H, 19in (482mm) W, 15.25in (388.45mm) D, 6RU"},"fan-left-is-never-empty":{"note":"REVERSED on the owner's observation, and the previous reasoning is kept in `fan-modules` below rather than deleted. `fan-left` carried an explicit `default: null` on the argument that Figure 1-7 calls the left strip a \"Secondary fan module slot (optional with redundancy kit)\", so a chassis without the kit shows an empty slot. The maintainer - \"I don't know if I've ever seen a C40G without something in that left slot\". Field observation beats an inference drawn from a schematic that draws both columns identically, and every image we hold agrees with him - Figures 1-1 and 1-7 and both front photographs show a module fitted on BOTH sides. WHAT IS STILL UNKNOWN is what a genuinely non-redundant chassis has there. A blank filler is the obvious candidate, and the guide lists \"Blank filler plates\" for rear slots 2 and 3 and never for this one. No figure shows the left slot empty, and none shows a fan blank. So the default is the fan module - the only occupant with a drawing - and this line is the record that the non-redundant case is unconfirmed rather than decided. WANTED - a photograph of a non-redundant C40G front, or a parts list naming a fan blank."},"fan-legend-layer":{"note":"UNRESOLVED, and the note below contradicts itself on it. It says the FAN TRAY 2 / FAN TRAY 1 / AIR FILTER legend is \"printed on the CHASSIS, which is why an empty left slot still shows it\" - but both front photographs show that legend clearly WITH a module fitted, and a chassis legend would be covered by the module sitting on it. So the legend travels with the module, or sits on a narrow fixed bezel inside the same column. The same question decides where the six slot numbers belong, which is why it matters. They are declared as device silkscreen at x 20, and L21 now reports all six as buried under `fan-left`, which spans x 1.5-36.2 and covers them. Measured off Figure 1-1 at 2.467 px/mm the left column divides into a grey strip 0.8-10.5, the pull handle 10.9-17.4, and a further band 17.8-37.3 that holds the numbers - and the RIGHT column measures the same 35-36 mm overall, so the bay extent itself is right and narrowing it would be wrong. What the images cannot resolve at this scale is whether that third band is module face or fixed bezel. ALL SEVEN C40G PHOTOGRAPHS were examined on 2026-08-27 and none of them settles it. What they do establish, and it is the most useful fact found: the two columns are NOT printed alike. At 9x on c40g-front-3x the LEFT column carries the hazard triangle AND the slot number in one continuous grey face with no seam between them, and the only seam is to the RIGHT of the number, against the card cage. The RIGHT column at the same magnification carries the triangle and NOTHING ELSE. That asymmetry is what argues the numbers are CHASSIS ink after all. Both bays accept the same casa/c40g-fan@1, so if the numbers rode on the module face the right-hand module would show them too, and it does not. The strip holding them must then be a fixed bezel at the inner edge of the left column, lying flush enough with the module face that no seam resolves at this resolution - which would make `fan-left` too wide rather than the numbers misplaced. That is a reading, not a measurement, and it is the opposite of what the photographs first suggested, so it is recorded as unresolved rather than acted on. c40g-empty-midplane-5x has every card out and both columns still fitted, at about 220 px across the column - too coarse to resolve the boundary or to see whether the numbers persist. c40g-lab-card-removal shows a seam in roughly the right place but at an angle that makes its position unusable. WANTED - one photograph of the C40G with the LEFT fan module withdrawn. If the numbers are still there, they are chassis ink and `fan-left` shrinks; if they leave with the module, they belong in a component skin and the two modules are different parts. Nothing else in the intake can decide it."},"fan-modules":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing - Figure 1-7, \"C40G fan module location and directional air flow\", settles which side is which and it is NOT symmetric. The RIGHT strip is labelled \"System fan module\" and \"Air filter\" with \"Air flow direction IN\"; the LEFT strip is labelled \"Secondary fan module slot (optional with redundancy kit)\" with \"Air flow direction OUT\". So fan-right defaults to a module and fan-left defaults to empty, which is what a chassis without the redundancy kit actually looks like. Both strips carry the same FAN TRAY 2 / FAN TRAY 1 / AIR FILTER legend printed on the CHASSIS, which is why an empty left slot still shows it in the guide figures"},"front-furniture":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing-measured - Figure 1-1, \"Casa C40G CMTS front view\", PASSES the orthographic gate. Its chassis renders 1364 x 760 px for an aspect of 1.795 against a true rack face of 482 / 265.9 = 1.813, agreeing to 1 percent, so unlike the isolated card figures it carries geometry - at 2.858 px/mm scaled by the exactly known 265.9 height. Measured off it in body coordinates: the two vertical fan strips at x 1.5-37.5 and 386.7-422.7, both running y 17-222; the card band x 37.5-386.4, which independently confirms the existing card bays at x 42.0 width 345.5; the brand band y 196.3-222.9; and the snap-on PSU cover y 226.7-264.9. The right fan bay is trimmed to start at x 388.0 so it does not overlap the card bays, which end at 387.5"},"non-redundant-variant":{"confidence":"drawing","note":"drawing plus prose - ADDED, because the guide draws four rear views and the model only had three configurations for them. Figures 1-2 and 1-4 are the AC and DC NON-REDUNDANT rears and 1-3 and 1-5 the redundant pair, so the four figures are two axes crossed - AC/DC and redundant/not - not four layouts. The AC/DC axis was already modelled as ac-power; this entry adds the other value of the second axis.
